v.rationale:
All three have the same overall structure: a cutoff scope, dry-run before the confirmation, a cache lock with try/finally, a scheduled `--force` run on one server, and a local disk with throw=false. They differ in the details.

impl-1 has the most idiomatic and efficient purge loop: chunkById, then partition, then one bulk delete per chunk, plus ConfirmableTrait. It also has the most thorough tests, covering confirm yes and no, the non-interactive refusal and retry on the next run. Its weakness is that the file delete isn't wrapped in a try/catch. This only matters if the disk throws; the shipped config doesn't, but one setting change would make it stop at the first failure.

impl-2 handles failures most robustly (catches Throwable) and its operations are thorough: a 6h lock TTL plus withoutOverlapping. Its tests are solid. Against it: it hand-rolls the confirmation instead of using ConfirmableTrait, and it deletes one row per query.

impl-3 uses ConfirmableTrait and safe exception handling. It ranks last because of the short 1h lock TTL on a multi-million-row job with no schedule-level overlap guard, a hard-coded timezone nobody asked for, by-reference closure counters, brittle anonymous-class disk fakes, and no test that confirming 'yes' proceeds.

impl-1 and impl-2 are close. impl-1 edges ahead because its code and tests make better use of the framework.
